entities.name: Adrianus Sunarko
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adrianus Sunarko OFM (born 1968) is an Indonesian Franciscan friar and Roman Catholic bishop who has served as Bishop of Pangkalpinang on the island of Bangka in Indonesia. His appointment reflects the global expansion of the Catholic episcopate in Southeast Asia, where the Church is a minority faith in a predominantly Muslim nation yet maintains significant institutional presence through its educational and healthcare networks.

Indonesia is the world's most populous Muslim-majority nation, and its Catholic community — approximately 3% of the population — exists in a complex plural religious environment. Indonesian Catholicism has strong institutional roots particularly in education and healthcare, and the Church has generally maintained constructive relations with the Indonesian state and Islamic majority under the framework of Pancasila — the national ideology of unity in diversity.

Sunarko's Franciscan formation emphasises mission to the poor and the margins, priorities that resonate with the pastoral challenges of a diocese serving the Bangka island mining region where social inequalities and environmental damage from tin mining create significant pastoral demands. His academic background in theology has also contributed to Indonesian Catholic intellectual life. His bishop's role requires maintaining the Church's minority presence with both pastoral creativity and institutional prudence.
